description: CREATE STREAM ON VIEW where the view is a UNION ALL over single-table branches. Snowflake's change tracking supports projections, filters and UNION ALL - each branch tracked INDEPENDENTLY on its own base table - while plain UNION, joins and other set operators stay rejected. Pinned: a stream's SELECT * yields the source's data columns FIRST and then METADATA$ACTION, METADATA$ISUPDATE, METADATA$ROW_ID in Snowflake's order (and an explicit column list still resolves the metadata columns by name); both UNION ALL branches surface their inserts; each branch applies its OWN WHERE filter to its own base table's changes; and look-alike rows in different branches do NOT cross-cancel, because the net-delta consolidation is scoped per source table - a literal per branch proves which branch's row survived an insert-plus-delete in the other. Converted 1:1 from stream/StreamOnUnionViewTest (now retired); the last test carried an Assumptions.assumeFalse(isLiveSnowflake()) because it matches frostlake's own rejection wording for a join inside a UNION ALL arm, a mixed shape unmeasured on a real account (single-branch inner-join views ARE supported - see stream-on-join-view), so it becomes skip snowflake with that reason kept.

steps.sql: CREATE STREAM st ON TABLE st_src
CREATE TABLE t1 (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE t2 (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
CREATE VIEW u AS SELECT id, name FROM t1 UNION ALL SELECT id, name FROM t2
CREATE STREAM s ON VIEW u
SELECT id, name, METADATA$ACTION FROM s ORDER BY id
CREATE VIEW u AS SELECT id FROM t1 WHERE id > 10 UNION ALL SELECT id FROM t2 WHERE id < 100
CREATE STREAM s ON VIEW u
SELECT id FROM s ORDER BY id
CREATE VIEW u AS SELECT id, 'FROM_T1' AS src FROM t1 UNION ALL SELECT id, 'FROM_T2' AS src FROM t2
CREATE STREAM s ON VIEW u
SELECT id, src, METADATA$ACTION FROM s
CREATE VIEW u AS SELECT id FROM t1 UNION SELECT id FROM t2
CREATE STREAM s ON VIEW u

skip.reason: matches frostlake's rejection wording (change tracking supports ...) for a join inside a UNION ALL arm; single-branch inner-join views ARE supported (see stream-on-join-view) and this mixed shape is unmeasured on a real account

steps.sql: CREATE VIEW u AS SELECT t1.id FROM t1 JOIN t2 ON t1.id = t2.id UNION ALL SELECT id FROM t2
CREATE STREAM s ON VIEW u
